idiom_name: plain headers object plus a middleware wrapper (KafkaJS headers, amqplib properties.headers)
implementation_notes: Node clients carry metadata as a plain object - KafkaJS message headers (a string or an array of strings per key) and amqplib's msg.properties.headers - so the trail is one more key: a (msg, next) middleware function parses the JSON list, appends its own hop and re-encodes before the next handler publishes. Where RabbitMQ already tracks infrastructure hops, read msg.properties.headers['x-death'] (an array of {queue, reason, count, time} entries appended by the broker) instead of maintaining a parallel list; the classic OO structure of a history container with per-component hooks is replaced by a middleware function and one JSON value.
pitfalls: Rebuilding a message with a fresh headers object drops unknown keys - including x-death and vendor metadata other hops depend on; spread the incoming headers instead of replacing them.
KafkaJS header values may be strings or arrays of strings (and Buffer in other clients), so a code path that assumes a single string will corrupt or misread multi-value headers.
JSON.parse on a partner-supplied header throws on malformed input and happily parses a huge payload: guard with try/catch, validate the entry shape and cap the list length.
